'''Keilor Antonio Navas Gamboa''' ({{IPA|es|ˈkej.lor anˈto.njo ˈna.βas ɣamˈbo.a|lang}};<ref>{{cite web|date=23 March 2017|title=Entrevista a Keylor Navas - Portero Real Madrid|trans-title=Interview with Keylor Navas - Real Madrid Goalkeeper|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pNsicQ-iFKY&t=16s|access-date=22 February 2024|website=[[YouTube]]|publisher=Fútbol Emotion|language=es}}</ref> born 15 December 1986), known as '''Keylor Navas''', is a Costa Rican professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for and captains [[Liga MX]] club [[Pumas UNAM]] and the [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica national team]]. He is regarded as one of the best goalkeepers of his generation, and one of the greatest ever [[CONCACAF]] goalkeepers.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fernandez|first=Ileana|date=12 March 2023|title=Keylor Navas included in IFFHS men's all time world best goalkeeper ranking|url=https://ticotimes.net/2023/03/12/keylor-navas-included-in-iffhs-mens-all-time-world-best-goalkeeper-ranking|access-date=25 June 2024|work=[[The Tico Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=15 January 2021|title=Keylor Navas ranked among the best goalkeepers of the decade|last=Claro|first=Marco|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2021/01/15/6001eb34ca474191768b45d6.html|access-date=23 February 2026|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Sharpless|first=Hunter|date=29 July 2019|title=Real Madrid's Keylor Navas Is The Greatest Concacaf Goalkeeper Of All Time|url=https://www.flofc.com/articles/6542848-real-madrids-keylor-navas-is-the-greatest-concacaf-goalkeeper-of-all-time|access-date=25 June 2024|website=FloFC}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Rachini|first=Mouhamad|date=23 April 2020|title=The 50: Top 10 North & Central American goalkeepers of all time.|url=https://btsgoalies.com/2020/04/23/top-10-north-central-america-goalkeepers/|access-date=25 June 2024|website=Between the Sticks}}</ref>

Navas started his youth career at [[Deportivo Saprissa|Saprissa]] in his home country, where he won six [[Liga FPD]] titles. He subsequently moved to Spanish club [[Albacete Balompié|Albacete]] in 2010, and then to [[Levante UD|Levante]] in [[La Liga]] the following year, where he won the LFP Award for Best Goalkeeper in his final season with the latter club. Navas later joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2014 for €10 million, where he won a total of twelve titles,<ref name=realmadrid>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/the-club/history/football-legends/keylor-navas|title=Keylor Navas|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> including one [[La Liga]] and three consecutive [[UEFA Champions League]] titles as the first choice goalkeeper.<ref name=realmadrid/> In 2019, he was signed by French club [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]], and would play in his [[2020 UEFA Champions League final|fourth Champions League final]] in his first season with the side.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/madrid-and-psg-switch-goalkeepers-navas-and-areola|access-date=22 February 2026|date=4 March 2020|title=Madrid and PSG switch goalkeepers Navas and Areola|website=Fox Sports}}</ref>

Navas has made over 120 appearances for Costa Rica since debuting in 2008. He has represented the country at three [[CONCACAF Gold Cup]]s and the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]], [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]], and [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]] editions of the [[FIFA World Cup]]. He was a Costa Rica national team member who reached the semi-finals of the [[2009 CONCACAF Gold Cup|2009 Gold Cup]], in which he was named best goalkeeper. His impressive performances also helped the team reach the quarter-finals of the World Cup for the first time in 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12040/9373172/world-cup-costa-rica-hero-hails-nations-efforts-as-holland-end-journey|work=[[Sky Sports]]|title=World Cup: Costa Rica hero hails nation's efforts as Holland end journey|date=6 July 2014|access-date=6 July 2014}}</ref>

Navas was awarded [[CONCACAF Awards|CONCACAF Men's Goalkeeper of the Year]] for three consecutive years between [[2016 CONCACAF Awards|2016]] and [[2018 CONCACAF Awards|2018]]. He was also named the best male CONCACAF Player of the Decade by the [[International Federation of Football History & Statistics|IFFHS]].<ref name=iffhs>{{cite web|date=5 February 2021|url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-best-man-player-concacaf-of-the-decade-2011-2020-949|title=IFFHS Best Man Player - CONCACAF - Of the Decade 2011-2020|publisher=IFFHS|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> His performances in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2017–18 season]] earned him the [[UEFA Club Football Awards|2017–18 UEFA Club Football Award]] for [[Best European Goalkeeper|best UEFA goalkeeper]],<ref name=uefa1>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d81f6382091-b3a8b300ea0b-1000--keylor-navas-champions-league-goalkeeper-of-the-season/|title=Keylor Navas: Champions League Goalkeeper of the Season|publisher=UEFA|date=30 August 2018|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> and also saw him named in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League#Squad of the season|UEFA Champions League Squad of the Season]] of 2018.<ref name=uefa2>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d8222ae4584-fc81fa8bf4d6-1000--uefa-champions-league-squad-of-the-season/|title=UEFA Champions League Squad of the Season|publisher=UEFA|access-date=23 February 2026|date=30 August 2018}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Saprissa===
Born in [[San Isidro de El General]], [[Pérez Zeledón (canton)|Pérez Zeledón]], Navas made his professional debut with [[Deportivo Saprissa]] on 6 November 2005, in a [[Costa Rican Primera División|Primera league]] match against [[Asociación Deportiva Carmelita]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nacion.com/ln_ee/futbol/campeonato2005-2006/noviembre/07/sap_car.html|title=Juego apenas para el gasto |trans-title=I play only to make ends meet|publisher=La Nación|language=es|date=7 November 2005|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070813131145/http://www.nacion.com/ln_ee/futbol/campeonato2005-2006/noviembre/07/sap_car.html|archive-date=13 August 2007}}</ref> He was the first-choice keeper in his two final seasons with the club,<ref>{{cite web|title=¿En qué temporadas fue Keylor Navas titular en el Saprissa?|url=https://futbolcentroamerica.com/costarica/En-que-temporadas-fue-Keylor-Navas-titular-en-el-Saprissa-20220413-0005.html|access-date=13 April 2022|website=Fútbol Centroamérica|date=13 April 2022|language=es-ES}}</ref> winning six [[Liga FPD|national championships]] and the [[2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup]].<ref name=realmadrid/> Navas was also part of the Saprissa team that finished in 3rd place at the [[2005 FIFA Club World Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/archive/japan2005/clubs/club=1896632/matches.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151025132222/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/archive/japan2005/clubs/club=1896632/matches.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 October 2015|title=Fifa Club World Championship Toyota Cup Japan 2005 - Clubs - Saprissa|publisher=[[FIFA]]|access-date=6 February 2019}}</ref>

===Albacete===
In July 2010, Navas signed with [[Albacete Balompié]] of the [[Segunda División]] in [[Spain]] precisely 20 years after countryman [[Luis Gabelo Conejo|Luis Conejo]], who occupied the same position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.albacetebalompie.es/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=447:navas-qvengo-con-mucho-compromisoq&catid=43:ultimas-noticias&Itemid=117|title=Navas: "Vengo con mucho compromiso"|trans-title=Navas: "I come full of commitment"|publisher=Albacete's official website|language=es|date=9 July 2010|access-date=27 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029195753/https://www.albacetebalompie.es/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=447:navas-qvengo-con-mucho-compromisoq&catid=43:ultimas-noticias&Itemid=117|archive-date=29 October 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> He played in 36 games out of 42 during [[2010–11 Segunda División|his first season]], but his team suffered relegation after finishing in last position.

===Levante===
[[File:Keylor Navas.jpg|thumb|right|165px|Navas playing for [[Levante UD|Levante]] in 2013]]
In the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12 campaign]], Navas reached [[La Liga]], being loaned to [[Levante UD]] for a year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fichajes.net/noticias/keylor-navas-cedido-al-levante-20110702.html|title=Keylor Navas, cedido al Levante|trans-title=Keylor Navas, loaned to Levante|publisher=Fichajes|language=es|date=2 July 2011|access-date=28 February 2014}}</ref> He made his debut in the competition on 13 May 2012 in the last round, playing in a 3–0 home win against [[Athletic Bilbao]] that confirmed the club's first ever [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|qualification]] for the [[UEFA Europa League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/323688/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Ghezzal helps Levante secure European place|publisher=[[ESPN Soccernet]]|date=13 May 2012|access-date=27 October 2013}}</ref> and joined the Valencian club on a three-year contract in July of that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/07/07/futbol/equipos/levante/1341656131.html|title=Keylor Navas ficha por el Levante|trans-title=Keylor Navas signs for Levante|work=Marca|language=es|date=7 July 2012|access-date=27 October 2013}}</ref> Despite initially being back-up to [[Gustavo Munúa]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aldia.cr/futbol-costa-rica/legionarios/Keylor_Navas-Levante-Gustavo_Munua-contrato-titular_0_110388964.html|title=Keylor Navas ante su oportunidad en el Levante si Gustavo Munúa deja el equipo|trans-title=Keylor Navas before his chance at Levante if Gustavo Munúa leaves team|publisher=Al Día|language=es|date=3 April 2013|access-date=28 February 2014}}</ref> Navas was the first-choice goalkeeper for Levante in the 2013–14 season, and was nominated as the league's best goalkeeper alongside [[Thibaut Courtois]] of [[Atlético Madrid]] and [[Willy Caballero]] of [[Málaga CF]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Fernandez-Abascal|first=Eduardo|title=Chelsea Duo Thibaut Courtois And Filipe Luis Nominated For La Liga Awards|url=https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/chelsea-duo-thibaut-courtois-filipe-luis-nominated-la-liga-awards-1470026|access-date=15 October 2014|work=[[International Business Times]]|date=14 October 2014}}</ref> going on to win the prize.<ref name=premio>{{cite web|title=gala de premios LFP 2013/14|trans-title=LFP Awards show 2013/14|url=https://www.lfp.es/gala-lfp-2013-2014|publisher=[[Liga de Fútbol Profesional]]|access-date=10 November 2014|language=es|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141105051027/http://www.lfp.es/gala-lfp-2013-2014|archive-date=5 November 2014}}</ref> In March 2014, he was [[La Liga Player of the Month]], the first goalkeeper to win the accolade.<ref name=lfp>{{cite news|title=Premios BBVA a los mejores de marzo|trans-title=BBVA awards for the best in March|url=https://www.laliga.com/noticias/premios-bbva-a-los-mejores-de-marzo|access-date=23 February 2026|publisher=[[Liga de Fútbol Profesional]]|date=7 April 2014|language=es}}</ref> He finished the season as the goalkeeper with the most saves (267) in La Liga,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://foxsports.com/soccer/stats?competition=2&season=20130&category=OVERALL|title=2013–14 La Liga Statistics and Leaders: Overall|work=Fox Sports|date=30 June 2014|access-date=7 July 2018}}</ref> finishing fourth in the [[2013–14 La Liga|Zamora Trophy]] conceding 39 goals in 36 games despite playing for a 'lower ranked' team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/trofeos/2013-2014/pichichi-zamora/zamora-primera.html|title=Tropheo Pichichi Liga Adelante|work=Marca|date=30 June 2014|access-date=7 July 2018}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:Real Madrid.JPG|thumb|left|270px|Navas giving directions to Real Madrid's defence.]]

====2014–15====
On 3 August 2014, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] triggered Navas' €10 million buyout clause,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/aug/03/real-madrid-confirm-keylor-navas-signing|title=Real Madrid confirm signing of Costa Rica's goalkeeper Keylor Navas|agency=Press Association|date=3 August 2014|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=14 September 2017|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> and he signed a six-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-statement-keylor-navas|title=Official statement: Keylor Navas|date=3 August 2014|website=Realmadrid.com|access-date=5 August 2014|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140805065726/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-statement-keylor-navas}}</ref> His first competitive call-up was on 12 August, sitting on the bench as [[Iker Casillas]] played in the [[2014 UEFA Super Cup]], which Real Madrid won 2–0 against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] at the [[Cardiff City Stadium]].<ref name=super>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28741099|last=Phillips|first=Rob|title=Super Cup: Cristiano Ronaldo scores twice in Real Madrid win|access-date=13 August 2014|work=BBC Sport|date=12 August 2014}}</ref> Navas was given his debut for the club on 23 September, in a 5–1 victory over [[Elche CF|Elche]] at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Sámano|first=José|title=Insaciable Cristiano|trans-title=Insatiable Cristano|work=[[El País]]|access-date=19 May 2015|url=https://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2014/09/23/actualidad/1411484192_802912.html|date=23 September 2014|language=es}}</ref> He was given his [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] debut on 26 November, keeping a clean sheet in a 0–1 away win against Swiss side [[FC Basel]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/29363787|title=FC Basel 0-1 Real Madrid|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 November 2014|access-date=18 September 2019}}</ref> On 20 December, he was on the bench as his team won the [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup|Club World Cup]], defeating [[Club Atlético San Lorenzo]] in [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup Final|the final]] in Morocco.<ref name=world>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid beat San Lorenzo to take Club World Cup crown|url=https://www.espnfc.co.uk/fifa-club-world-cup/match/409204/real-madrid-san-lorenzo/report|access-date=22 June 2015|work=ESPN FC|date=20 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706004327/https://www.espnfc.co.uk/fifa-club-world-cup/match/409204/real-madrid-san-lorenzo/report|archive-date=6 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> His performances for Levante in the previous La Liga season and [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]] in the 2014 World Cup led him win Player of the Year at the [[2014 CONCACAF Awards]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fichajes.net/noticias/keylor-navas-cedido-al-levante-20110702.html|title=Keylor Navas es el mejor portero del 2014 en la Concacaf|trans-title=Keylor Navas is the best goalkeeper of 2014 of Concacaf|publisher=El Comercio|language=es|date=2 July 2011|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> earning the dual distinction of the first Costa Rican and goalkeeper to do so.

====2015–16====
[[File:Keylor Navas en el Real Madrid.JPG|thumb|right|Navas with Real Madrid in 2016]]
With the departure of Casillas from Real Madrid, Navas inherited his number 1 shirt for the [[2015–16 La Liga]] season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2015/07/19/13720702/navas-takes-casillas-no1-jersey-at-madrid|title=Navas takes Casillas' No.1 jersey at Madrid|date=19 July 2015|access-date=20 July 2015|website=Goal.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721195356/https://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2015/07/19/13720702/navas-takes-casillas-no1-jersey-at-madrid|archive-date=21 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Madrid agreed to transfer Navas to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in part-exchange for [[David de Gea]] on 31 August 2015. Still, the deal collapsed because the documents were not submitted to [[FIFA]] before the Spanish transfer deadline.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34117354|title=David De Gea: Real Madrid 'did everything' to sign Man Utd keeper|work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=1 September 2015|access-date=1 September 2015}}</ref>

Madrid thrashed [[Real Betis]] in their home opener by a score of 5–0 with a fine performance from Navas, making several saves and stopping a penalty.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/08/5-0-spectacular-display-of-firepower-in-the-bernabeus-la-liga-opener|title=5–0: Spectacular display of firepower in the Bernabéu's La Liga opener|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=30 August 2015|access-date=7 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180707202027/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/08/5-0-spectacular-display-of-firepower-in-the-bernabeus-la-liga-opener|archive-date=7 July 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a regular starter when the team won the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]]. Navas earned the dual distinction of becoming the first Costa Rican and Central American ever to play in and win the men's Champions League final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://ticotimes.net/2016/05/28/keylor-navas-makes-history-champions-league|title=Keylor Navas makes history as Real Madrid wins Champions League title|publisher=The Tico Times|date=28 May 2016|access-date=19 July 2018}}</ref> He set a new record for Real Madrid in the [[UEFA Champions League]] by not conceding a single goal in his first eight appearances; 6 of these were in the 2015–16 season. He also usurped [[Edwin van der Sar]] to reach the second spot in clean sheets behind [[Jens Lehmann]] in the all-time list. He was the best goalkeeper in the 2015–16 UEFA Champions League season, conceding only three goals in 12 appearances, keeping nine clean sheets.<ref name="2015–16 CL">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|date=28 May 2016|publisher=[[UEFA]]|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

====2016–17====
He was the starting goalkeeper when Madrid won the [[2016–17 La Liga]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|date=21 May 2017|work=laliga.es|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Real Madrid win La Liga title with victory at Malaga|date=21 May 2017|work=BBC|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> and the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League]].<ref name=Cardiff>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|date=3 June 2017|work=[[UEFA]]|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> On 29 January 2017 after the 3–0 win at home to Real Sociedad in La Liga, Navas became the first player from Costa Rica to reach 100 La Liga appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/optajose/status/825804208523923458|title=100 – Keylor Navas is the first player from Costa Rica to reach 100 appearances in La Liga history. Tico.|publisher=OptaJose|date=29 January 2017|access-date=13 July 2018}}</ref> His performances during the double trophy-winning season led him to win the Player of the Year for the second time at the [[2017 CONCACAF Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/12/keylor-navas-concacaf-player-of-the-year|title=Keylor Navas, Concacaf player of the year|publisher=Real Madrid|date=18 December 2017|access-date=7 July 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180707172742/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/12/keylor-navas-concacaf-player-of-the-year|archive-date=7 July 2018}}</ref>

====2017–18====
Navas made his 100th appearance for Madrid during the [[2017 Supercopa de España|2–0]] second-leg home win over [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/08/keylor-navas-100-games-for-real-madrid|title=Keylor Navas, 100 games for Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid|date=16 August 2017|access-date=14 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714171417/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/08/keylor-navas-100-games-for-real-madrid|archive-date=14 July 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]], he started eleven games, as Madrid won their third consecutive and 13th overall Champions League title beating [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] [[2018 UEFA Champions League Final|3–1]] in the final.<ref name=Kiev>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/|title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick|date=26 May 2018|work=[[UEFA]]|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> The win against Liverpool saw Navas claim his 100th victory for Madrid in only 141 appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/05/keylor-navas-claims-100th-win-in-a-real-madrid-shirt|title=Keylor Navas claims 100th win in a Real Madrid shirt|publisher=Real Madrid|date=26 May 2018|access-date=13 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713231216/https://realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/05/keylor-navas-claims-100th-win-in-a-real-madrid-shirt|archive-date=13 July 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Navas produced some fine performances in the Champions League including a superb display against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in their [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|semi-final]] second leg clash which helped Real Madrid qualify to the final. He made eight saves during the game, his highest tally in a Champions League knock-out game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/OptaJose/status/991418962419376129/photo/1|title=8 – Keylor Navas made eight saves against Bayern Munich, his highest tally in a Champions League knock-out game. Hero.|publisher=OptaJose|date=1 May 2018|access-date=19 July 2018}}</ref> Bayern Munich manager [[Jupp Heynckes]] praised Navas after the game as the reason for Real Madrid's qualification.<ref>{{cite news|last=Calderón|first=J. L.|url=https://marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/05/01/5ae8dffe468aeb13348b4663.html|title=Heynckes: Real Madrid can thank Keylor for their qualification|work=Marca|date=1 May 2018|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

====2018–19====
Navas’ fifth season at Real Madrid began with the much-anticipated arrival of [[Thibaut Courtois]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/08/08/5b686c67ca474125568b4766.html|title=Official: Real Madrid sign Courtois|work=Marca|date=8 August 2018|access-date=5 September 2018}}</ref> to compete for the number 1 goalkeeping spot. Despite Courtois’ arrival, Navas was selected to play in the [[2018 UEFA Super Cup]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/08/15/5b73ec6e268e3e535c8b4593.html|title=Keylor Navas remains the starter for now|last=Calderón|first=J. L.|work=Marca|date=15 August 2018|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> which resulted in a 2–4 loss to city rivals [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/r-madrid-vs-a-madrid/389371|title=Real Madrid 2–4 Atletico Madrid: Atleti win Super Cup thriller in extra-time|publisher=Sky Sports|date=16 August 2018|access-date=5 September 2018}}</ref> Navas then went on to start the opening game of [[2018–19 La Liga|La Liga]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2018/08/19/soccer/1534705628_708873.html|title=Real Madrid vs Getafe: Keylor Navas, Ceballos start for hosts|work=AS.com|publisher=AS|date=19 August 2018|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> comfortably keeping his first clean sheet of the season with a 2–0 win over [[Getafe CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/2-0-real-madrid-kick-off-laliga-campaign-with-deserved-win|title=2-0: Real Madrid kick off LaLiga campaign with deserved win|publisher=Real Madrid|date=19 August 2018|access-date=5 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180820105725/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/08/2-0-real-madrid-kick-off-laliga-campaign-with-deserved-win|archive-date=20 August 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> His performances in the last Champions League campaign led him to be voted as the [[UEFA Club Football Awards|2017–18 UEFA Champions League Goalkeeper of the Season]]<ref name=uefa1/> beating off competition from then [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] goalkeeper [[Alisson Becker]] and [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] goalkeeper [[Gianluigi Buffon]]. On 9 January 2019, Navas made his 150th appearance in all competitions for Madrid in their 3–0 home win against [[CD Leganés|Leganés]] in the [[2018–19 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/keylor-navas-makes-his-150th-real-madrid-appearance|title=Keylor Navas makes his 150th Real Madrid appearance|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=9 January 2019|access-date=14 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190114153357/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/keylor-navas-makes-his-150th-real-madrid-appearance|archive-date=14 January 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 6 April 2019 Navas became the first ever non-Spanish goalkeeper to reach 100 La Liga appearances for Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/04/keylor-navas-100-laliga-games-with-real-madrid|title=Keylor Navas: 100 LaLiga games with Real Madrid|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=6 April 2019|access-date=9 April 2019|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413132111/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/04/keylor-navas-100-laliga-games-with-real-madrid|archive-date=13 April 2019}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
Navas joined [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] (PSG) on a four-year contract on 2 September 2019,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/09/official-announcement-keylor-navas|title=Official Announcement: Keylor Navas|publisher=realmadrid.com|date=2 September 2019|access-date=2 September 2019}}</ref> becoming the first Costa Rican to play for the men's team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/keylor-navas-signs-four-year-deal-with-paris-saint-germain|title=Keylor Navas signs four year deal with Paris Saint-Germain|publisher=psg.fr|date=2 September 2019|access-date=2 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190902161227/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/keylor-navas-signs-four-year-deal-with-paris-saint-germain|archive-date=2 September 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his [[Ligue 1]] debut 12 days later, keeping a clean sheet in a 1–0 home win against [[RC Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/last-gasp-win|title=Last-gasp win!|publisher=en.psg.fr|date=14 September 2019|access-date=15 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200318182741/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/last-gasp-win|archive-date=18 March 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 24 July 2020, Navas won his 20th career club trophy after beating [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] in the [[2020 Coupe de France Final|Coupe de France]] final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://psgtalk.com/2020/07/navas-claims-20th-career-trophy-following-coupe-de-france-final-win/|title=Navas Claims 20th Career Trophy Following Coupe de France Final Win|publisher=PSGTalk|date=24 July 2020|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref> On 31 July, he kept a clean sheet and saved a spot kick in the resulting shoot-out as PSG defeated [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] 6–5 on penalties in the [[2020 Coupe de la Ligue Final]].<ref name="PSG win Coupe de la Ligue">{{cite web|url=https://www.thescore.com/fra_fed/news/1993801/amp|title=PSG win Coupe de la Ligue to complete domestic quadruple|publisher=theScore.com|last=Brunt|first=Gordon|date=31 July 2020|access-date=31 July 2020}}</ref> That win marked Navas' 15th trophy in Europe, matching [[Rafael Márquez]]'s record for a [[CONCACAF]] player.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/08/01/football/1596301925_443630.html|title=Keylor Navas equals Márquez's historic European trophy haul|publisher=AS|last=Serrano|first=Rodrigo|date=1 August 2020|access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref> On 23 August 2020, Navas started his 4th [[2020 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]], losing to Bayern Munich 1–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=573698|title=Bayern Munich beat Paris Saint-Germain to win Champions League|publisher=ESPN|date=23 August 2020|access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref> He finished the European campaign with 5 clean sheets, the second most after [[Manuel Neuer]] despite having played 191 minutes less.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.squawka.com/en/most-clean-sheets-champions-league-2019-2020-golden-gloves/|title=Most clean sheets: Champions League 2019/20 season final standings|publisher=Squawka|date=24 August 2020|access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref>

Navas started his second season with PSG as one of the seven club players to test positive for [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://ticotimes.net/2020/09/04/keylor-navas-among-psg-players-reported-to-have-coronavirus|title=Keylor Navas among PSG players reported to have coronavirus|publisher=Tico Times|date=4 September 2020|access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/paris-saint-germain/story/4175670/psgfrance-star-kylian-mbappe-tests-positive-for-coronavirus|title=PSG, France star Kylian Mbappe tests positive for coronavirus|publisher=ESPN|date=7 September 2020|access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref> He missed the clubs first two games due to the quarantine requirement.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54108520|title=Depleted PSG beaten by promoted Lens|publisher=BBC|date=10 September 2020|access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54141979|title=Five sent off as Marseille beat PSG|last=Begley|first=Emlyn|publisher=BBC|date=14 September 2020|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> On 16 September 2020, Navas played his first game of the season winning and keeping a clean sheet against [[FC Metz|Metz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54150578|title=Draxler's late goal earns PSG first win|publisher=BBC|date=16 September 2020|access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref> On 17 September, [[UEFA]] announced Navas, for the second time, as a nominee for the 2019–20 Champions League Goalkeeper of the Season award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0261-10657c4cbf33-3fc280ec8da7-1000--shortlist-of-nominees-for-2019-20-uefa-club-competition-awards-/|title=Shortlist of nominees for 2019/20 UEFA club competition awards revealed|publisher=UEFA|date=17 September 2020|access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref> On 20 September, Navas starred in PSG's 3–0 away win to [[OGC Nice|Nice]] with a second consecutive clean sheet as well as several excellent saves.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/ogc-nice-0-3-paris-saint-germain-parisians-player-ratings-kylian-mbappe-inspires-easy-win-ligue-1-2020-21|title=OGC Nice 0-3 Paris Saint-Germain-Parisians' player ratings as Kylian Mbappe inspires easy win-Ligue 1 2020-21|last=Sagar|first=Sunaadh|publisher=sportskeeda|date=20 September 2020|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> On 13 January 2021, Navas won the [[2020 Trophée des Champions]]. With that win, he became the CONCACAF player with the most European trophies, 16, surpassing former Rafael Márquez.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/01/14/soccer/1610587784_226565.html|title=Keylor Navas is the CONCACAF player with most European titles|publisher=AS|date=14 January 2021|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> On 20 April 2021, Navas was voted [[UNFP Player of the Month|Ligue 1 Player of the Month]] for March, making him the first CONCACAF player to win the award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/keylor-navas-named-ligue-1-player-of-the-month-for-march-paris-saint-germain-unfp|title=Keylor Navas named Ligue 1 player of the month for March|publisher=psg.com|date=22 April 2021|access-date=22 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422204801/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/keylor-navas-named-ligue-1-player-of-the-month-for-march-paris-saint-germain-unfp|archive-date=22 April 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref> Navas signed a contract with PSG until 2024 on 26 April 2021.<ref>{{cite web|date=26 April 2021|title=Keylor Navas extends his contract until 2024|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/keylor-navas-extends-his-paris-saint-germain-contract-until-2024#:~:text=Paris%20Saint%2DGermain%20is%20delighted,at%20the%202014%20World%20Cup.|access-date=1 June 2021|website=[[Paris Saint-Germain]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602214048/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/keylor-navas-extends-his-paris-saint-germain-contract-until-2024|archive-date=2 June 2021|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2021–22 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season|2021–22 season]], PSG signed Italian goalkeeper [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]]. This raised eyebrows over potential competition between Navas and his Italian counterpart.<ref>{{Cite web|date=16 September 2021|title=PSG: Will the competition between Navas and Donnarumma be a problem?|url=https://www.ruetir.com/2021/09/16/psg-will-the-competition-between-navas-and-donnarumma-be-a-problem/|access-date=22 September 2021|website=Ruetir|language=en-US|archive-date=22 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210922044231/https://www.ruetir.com/2021/09/16/psg-will-the-competition-between-navas-and-donnarumma-be-a-problem/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the [[2022–23 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season|2022–23 season]], new coach [[Christophe Galtier]] confirmed that Navas would occupy the position of number two goalkeeper.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bethsy|first=Eric|date=23 July 2022|title=PSG : Galtier calme Navas après sa démonstration|url=https://www.foot01.com/paris/psg-galtier-calme-navas-apres-sa-demonstration-408845|access-date=24 July 2022|website=Foot01|language=fr}}</ref>

====Loan to Nottingham Forest and return to PSG====
Following the long-term injury to [[Dean Henderson]], on 31 January 2023, Navas signed for [[Premier League]] club [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|date=31 January 2023|title=Keylor Navas joins Nottingham Forest on loan|url=https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/keylor-navas-paris-saint-germain-joins-nottingham-forest-fc-on-loan|access-date=31 January 2023|publisher=[[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230131235417/https://en.psg.fr/teams/first-team/content/keylor-navas-paris-saint-germain-joins-nottingham-forest-fc-on-loan|archive-date=31 January 2023|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut for Forest on 5 February, keeping a clean sheet in a 1–0 win over [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], and was named player of the match.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-soccer-leeds-united-brennan-johnson-keylor-navas-09d9c696f57dad5cfe4113d1cf1fda09|title=Keylor Navas stars on debut as Forest beats Leeds 1-0 in EPL|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=5 February 2023|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

Following his return to PSG, Navas was included in the Champions League squad for the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|2023–24 season]], having rejected a transfer to Saudi club [[Al Hilal SFC|Al Hilal]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Sévérac|first=Dominique|url=https://www.leparisien.fr/sports/football/psg/mercato-keylor-navas-reste-finalement-au-psg-pourquoi-luis-enrique-sen-frotte-les-mains-07-09-2023-TZMYKYOG6JHQJPHG72MSNXNVUI.php?ts=1694094908817|title=Mercato : Keylor Navas reste finalement au PSG, pourquoi Luis Enrique s'en frotte les mains|publisher=Le Parisien|language=fr|date=7 September 2023|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> On 11 May 2024, he announced his departure from PSG at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|date=11 May 2024|title=«Chaque seconde passée au Parc des Princes a été merveilleuse» : Navas va quitter le PSG|last=Remise|first=Christophe|url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/sports/football/ligue-1/psg-apres-mbappe-le-gardien-keylor-navas-annonce-son-depart-du-club-20240511|access-date=23 February 2026|website=Le Figaro|language=fr}}</ref>
[[File:Keylor Navas UNAM.jpg|thumb|Navas playing for [[Pumas UNAM|Pumas]] in 2025]]

===Newell's Old Boys===
On January 21, 2025, Navas joined [[Newell's Old Boys]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web|title=Keylor Navas: Former Real Madrid goalkeeper joins Newell's Old Boys|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6074790/2025/01/22/keylor-navas-transfer-newells-old-boys/|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=22 January 2025|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> A month later, on 2 February, he made his debut in a 1–0 win against [[Club Atlético Aldosivi|Aldosivi]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ticotimes.net/2025/02/03/costa-ricas-keylor-navas-shines-in-debut-for-newells-old-boys|title=Costa Rica's Keylor Navas Shines In Debut for Newell’s Old Boys|publisher=Tico Times|date=3 February 2025|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

In June 2025 Navas began to seek his departure from the team due to relationship problems with the coaching staff and fans of Newell's, which made him request not to play in the first matches of the [[2025 Argentine Primera División#Torneo Clausura|2025 Clausura Tournament]], while asking the club to allow him to be transferred to another team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aficionados argentinos revientan a Keylor Navas por ausentarse con Newell’s nuevamente: ‘Que se quede a cortar el pasto'|url=https://www.mediotiempo.com/futbol/liga-mx/aficionados-argentinos-molestos-keylor-navas-ausencia-newells-vs-banfield|website=Mediotiempo.com|access-date=22 July 2025|language=es|date=20 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Newell's anunció la salida de Keylor Navas y lo dejó expuesto con un durísimo comunicado|url=https://tn.com.ar/deportes/futbol/2025/07/22/newells-anuncio-la-salida-de-keylor-navas-y-lo-dejo-expuesto-con-un-durisimo-comunicado/|website=tn.com.ar|access-date=22 July 2025|language=es|date=21 July 2025}}</ref> 

After several weeks of failed sale negotiations,<ref>{{cite web|title=Newell's rechaza la primera oferta formal de Pumas por Keylor Navas|url=https://mexico.as.com/futbol/futbol-mexicano/newells-rechaza-la-primera-oferta-formal-de-pumas-por-keylor-navas-n/|website=AS México|access-date=22 July 2025|language=es|date=14 July 2025}}</ref> Newell's announced Navas's departure from the club on July 21, 2025, six months after joining the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Keylor Navas se va de Newell’s tras los conflictos con el club: la reacción de Fabbiani y los arqueros que podrían reemplazarlo|url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2025/07/21/keylor-navas-se-va-de-newells-tras-los-conflictos-con-el-club-la-reaccion-de-fabbiani-y-los-arqueros-que-podrian-reemplazarlo/|website=Infobae|access-date=22 July 2025|language=es|date=21 July 2025}}</ref>

===Pumas===
On 24 July 2025, [[Liga MX]] club [[Pumas UNAM|Pumas]] officially announced the signing of Navas.<ref>{{cite web|title=Newell's Old Boys hace oficial fichaje de Keylor Navas con Pumas|url=https://www.tudn.com/futbol/liga-mx/newells-old-boys-hace-oficial-fichaje-keylor-navas-pumas|last=Marroquín|first=Emmanuel R.|website=TUDN|access-date=23 February 2026|language=es|date=21 July 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth career and early senior career===
Navas was part of the Costa Rica national team that played in the [[2003 FIFA U-17 World Championship]] held in [[Finland]]. He was called up for the [[Costa Rica national football team|senior national team]] for the first time in August 2006 to play a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] tournament in Europe against [[Austria national football team|Austria]] and [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]]. He was a team member who won a bronze medal at the [[Football at the 2006 Central American and Caribbean Games|2006 Central American and Caribbean Games]]. Navas gained his debut senior [[Cap (sport)|cap]] on 11 October 2008, in a 4–1 away victory over [[Suriname national football team|Suriname]] in [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification – CONCACAF third round|the third round of stuff]] for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], which qualified the team into the next stage.<ref>{{cite news|title=Con el primer boleto|trans-title=With the first ticket|url=https://www.espn.cl/futbol/cronica?id=244641|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=ESPN|date=11 October 2008|language=es}}</ref> Four days later at the [[Estadio Ricardo Saprissa Aymá|Estadio Ricardo Saprissa]], he kept his first international clean sheet in a 2–0 victory over [[Haiti national football team|Haiti]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Sigue enrachado|trans-title=Carry on being lucky|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/futbol/cronica?id=244645|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=ESPN|date=15 October 2008|language=es}}</ref> The team eventually reached the [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (inter-confederation play-offs)|intercontinental play-offs]] for the tournament, losing narrowly to [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Uruguay 1 Costa Rica 1, agg 2–1: match report|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/6603766/Uruguay-1-Costa-Rica-1-agg-2-1-match-report.html|access-date=23 August 2015|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=19 November 2009}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Navas was also a member of the Costa Rica squad that finished runners-up in the [[2009 UNCAF Nations Cup]].<ref name="2009 UNCAF Nations Cup">{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesg/gold-cam09det.html|title=UNCAF (Qualifying Tournament for Gold Cup) 2009 - Details|website=[[RSSSF]]|last=Courtney|first=Barrie|date=19 June 2009|access-date=4 September 2019}}</ref>

Navas appeared with ''Los Ticos'' in two [[CONCACAF Gold Cup]] competitions, being named the best goalkeeper in the [[2009 CONCACAF Gold Cup|2009 edition]] as he helped his country reach the semi-finals.<ref name=best/> He returned to allow them to the quarter-finals [[2011 CONCACAF Gold Cup|two years later]], in what is to date his last appearance at a Gold Cup, as he would miss the tournament for the following ten years, a period that encompasses five editions.<ref>{{cite news|title=Keylor Navas cumple diez años sin jugar en una Copa Oro|url=https://www.espn.co.cr/futbol/costa-rica/nota/_/id/8831593/keylor-navas-cumple-diez-anos-sin-jugar-copa-oro|access-date=29 November 2022|work=ESPN.com.mx|date=26 June 2021|language=es}}</ref> He also missed the [[Copa América Centenario]] similarly.<ref>{{cite news|title=Confirman baja de Keylor Navas para la Copa América|url=https://www.dw.com/es/confirman-baja-de-keylor-navas-para-la-copa-am%C3%A9rica/a-19294796|access-date=29 November 2022|work=DW.COM|date=31 May 2016|language=es-ES}}</ref>

===2014 World Cup===
[[File:Uruguay - Costa Rica FIFA World Cup 2014 (27).jpg|thumb|175px|left|Navas and [[Giancarlo González]] celebrating Costa Rica's victory over Uruguay at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]]]]
Navas made his debut in the [[FIFA World Cup]] on 14 June 2014, appearing in a [[2014 FIFA World Cup|3–1 group stage win]] against [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] in [[Fortaleza]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=costa-rica-revival-undoes-uruguay-2370955.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140616044444/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=costa-rica-revival-undoes-uruguay-2370955.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 June 2014|title=Costa Rican comeback undoes Uruguay|publisher=FIFA.com|date=14 June 2014|access-date=16 June 2014}}</ref> and started the other two group games only conceding a single goal as Costa Rica qualified for the knockout stages as group winners<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/113597/keylor-navas-a-draw-against-england-isnt-bad-at-all/|title=Keylor Navas: A draw against England isn't bad at all|publisher=Inside Spanish Football|date=24 June 2014|access-date=29 June 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140629040555/http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/113597/keylor-navas-a-draw-against-england-isnt-bad-at-all/|archive-date=29 June 2014}}</ref> for the first time.

On 29 June, in the [[Single-elimination tournament|round of 16]] match against [[Greece national football team|Greece]], Navas was named [[man of the match]] after several saves in normal time and a save from [[Theofanis Gekas]]' kick during the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]], which led to Costa Rica reaching the quarter-finals for the first time ever.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/round=255951/match=300186459/match-report.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140701183741/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/round=255951/match=300186459/match-report.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 July 2014|title=Navas-inspired Ticos win shootout, reach quarters|publisher=FIFA.com|date=29 June 2014|access-date=30 June 2014}}</ref> He ended the tournament with three [[Shutout|clean sheets]] from five matches, as the country was knocked out by the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]] after a penalty shootout,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28069208|last=Chase|first=Graham|title=Netherlands 0–0 Costa Rica|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=5 June 2014|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> where he was named man of the match for the third time, the only goalkeeper to do so.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/brazil2014/awards/man-of-the-match/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622011229/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/brazil2014/awards/man-of-the-match/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 June 2015|title=Man of the Match|work=[[FIFA]]|access-date=6 February 2019}}</ref> He was also one of three nominees for the [[FIFA World Cup awards#Golden Glove|Golden Glove Award]], losing out to [[Manuel Neuer]] of Germany.<ref>{{cite news|last=Burrows|first=Ben|title=World Cup Golden Glove: Manuel Neuer, Sergio Romero and Keylor Navas nominated for award|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup-2014/world-cup-golden-glove-manuel-3845177|access-date=22 June 2015|publisher=[[Daily Mirror]]|date=11 July 2014}}</ref>

===2018 FIFA World Cup===
[[File:Bra-Cos (10).jpg|thumb|175px|right|Navas during Costa Rica's [[2018 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] match against Brazil in 2018.]]
In May 2018, Navas was named in the final [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/fifa-world-cup/news/costa-rica-names-23-man-world-cup-squad-featuring-keylor-navas/1k8gykq23stfg1ozewlah6cl9l|last=Arnold|first=John|title=Keylor Navas & six MLS players named in Costa Rica's 23-man World Cup squad|publisher=Sporting News|date=14 May 2018|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> He started all three group games, making ten saves and conceding five goals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/keylor-navas-player-news|title=Keylor Navas|work=Fox Sports|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

===2022 FIFA World Cup===
In November 2022, Navas was named in the final [[2022 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]] for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]]<ref>{{cite web|date=14 November 2022|title=Costa Rica Squad For FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 And Players List, Position|url=https://www.sportsunfold.com/costa-rica-squad-for-fifa-world-cup-qatar-2022-and-players-list-position/|access-date=24 November 2022|website=SportsUnfold|language=en-US}}</ref> In Costa Rica's first game against [[Spain national football team|Spain]], Navas conceded seven goals.<ref>{{cite news|date=23 November 2022|title=Photos: Spain's stars dazzle in 7-0 demolition of Costa Rica|last1=Furcoi|first1=Sorin|last2=Arciszewski|first2=Wojtek|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2022/11/23/photos-spains-stars-dazzle-in-7-0-thumping-of-costa-rica|access-date=23 February 2026|website=www.aljazeera.com}}</ref> In the second game of group play against [[Japan national football team|Japan]], Navas kept a clean sheet giving Costa Rica a surprise 1–0 win over their opponent.<ref>{{cite news|last=Porzio|first=Francesco|title=Japan vs. Costa Rica final score, FIFA World Cup 2022: Ticos get unexpected victory thanks to Keysher Fuller|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/japan-vs-costa-rica-final-score-fifa-world-cup-2022-ticos-get-unexpected-victory-thanks-to-keysher-fuller/|access-date=23 February 2026|agency=CBS Sports|date=28 November 2022}}</ref> Navas would lose 4–2 in Costa Rica's third group game against [[Germany national football team|Germany]]. ''Los Ticos'' finished fourth in their group with three points and a goal difference of –8.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/633827|title=Costa Rica vs. Germany - Football Match Summary|publisher=ESPN|date=1 December 2022|access-date=16 January 2023}}</ref>

===Retirement and return===
Navas played his last international match on 26 March 2024 in a friendly against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Argentina 3-1 Costa Rica (Mar 26, 2024) Final Score|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/699140/costa-rica-argentina|access-date=16 August 2024|website=ESPN}}</ref> On 23 May 2024, Navas announced his retirement from the national team.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cordoba|first=Javier|date=23 May 2024|title=Navas announces his retirement from the Costa Rica national team after 16 years and 3 World Cups|url=https://apnews.com/article/navas-costa-rica-soccer-retirement-60b0db8653068756938aa5a12e173b31|agency=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

In May 2025, he announced his return to international football and was subsequently included in Costa Rica's squad for the [[2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup]] by head coach [[Miguel Herrera]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/latam/deportivo/IDMSJVI5QJNIPMCAL7VC75ATW4-2025-05-23/|title=Keylor Navas regresa a selección de Costa Rica tras un año de ausencia|agency=[[Reuters]]|language=es|date=23 May 2025|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Often rated by several pundits as one of the best goalkeepers in the world,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/the-worlds-best-goalkeeper-2017-gianluigi-buffon-makes-it-491|title=The World's Best Goalkeeper 2017: Gianluigi Buffon Makes It Five!|publisher=IFFHS|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/thibaut-courtois-still-crowned-226|title=Thibaut Courtois Still Crowned!|publisher=IFFHS|access-date=22 February 2026}}</ref> and considered by some in the sport as the best in the history of CONCACAF,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diez.hn/blogs/keylor_navas-concacaf-mejor-portero-historia-CIDZ1077115#image-1|title=Keylor Navas es el mejor portero de la historia de CONCACAF|publisher=www.diez.hn|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> Navas is an energetic keeper, who is primarily known for his agility, speed, and athleticism in goal, as well as his quick reflexes and excellent shot-stopping ability, which enables him to compensate for his relative lack of height. He has also drawn praise in the media for his decisive performances in essential matches, and his penchant for producing difficult and crucial saves for his team in critical moments.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2016/05/27/574863ae22601d850a8b45dc.html|title=Navas' agility vs Oblak's reliability|work=Marca|last=Ortego|first=Enrique|last2=Winterburn|first2=Chris|date=27 May 2016|access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2802528-the-evolution-of-the-goalkeeper#slide1|title=The Evolution of the Goalkeeper: What Makes the Perfect Modern-Day No. 1?|publisher=Bleacher Report|last=Tighe|first=Sam|date=5 November 2018|access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thescore.com/chlg/news/1289056|title=Perfect player series: Building a flawless goalkeeper|publisher=The Score|last=Nesci|first=Gianluca|date=24 July 2017|access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1955860-scouting-report-is-levantes-keylor-navas-the-best-goalkeeper-in-europe|title=Scouting Report: Is Levante's Keylor Navas the Best Goalkeeper in Europe?|publisher=Bleacher Report|last=Jiang|first=Allan|date=11 February 2014|access-date=11 March 2020}}</ref> In 2017, former goalkeeper [[Manuel Almunia]] praised Navas, describing him as "the prototype model" goalkeeper, also adding: "He's spectacular between the posts, he's brave, skillful and very agile. He maintains his concentration, and he's also intelligent... For me, he deserves all the respect he gets for what he's done."<ref name="Kepa is good with his feet">{{cite web|url=https://en.as.com/en/2017/12/13/soccer/1513169565_572541.html|title=Manuel Almunia: "Kepa is good with his feet, like Luis Arconada"|last=Ruiz|first=Marco|work=AS.com|date=13 December 2017|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

In 2020, Navas cited compatriot [[Léster Morgan]] as his goalkeeping idol.<ref>{{cite news|last=Gómez|first=Keish|title=Keylor Navas recuerda nostálgico a su ídolo de la infancia, Lester Morgan|url=https://www.espn.co.cr/futbol/costa-rica/nota/_/id/6897559/keylor-navas-lester-morgan-idolo-infancia-futbol-costa-rica|access-date=30 April 2020|work=ESPN Costa Rica|date=29 April 2020|language=es}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Keylor Navas was raised in a low-income family in [[San Isidro de El General]], a town in the southeast of [[San José Province|San José province]]. He is a devout [[Christianity|Christian]]. He spoke about his faith, saying, "God for me comes first. Before every game, I kneel, open my arms, and pray ... My favorite passage of the Bible is [[Epistle to the Galatians|Galatians]] 1:10, which says: "If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a servant of Christ."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.efe.com/efe/english/entertainment/real-madrid-goalie-keylor-navas-weds-in-costa-rica/50000264-2645262|title=Real Madrid goalie Keylor Navas weds in Costa Rica}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jun/28/world-cup-2014-costa-rica-greece-keylor-navas-goalkeeper|title=World Cup 2014: Costa Rica's Keylor Navas is the man Greece must beat|last=Lowe|first=Sid|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=28 June 2014|access-date=29 June 2014}}</ref> On 3 December 2014, Navas announced that he had obtained Spanish citizenship.<ref>{{cite web|title=Keylor Navas now has Spanish citizenship|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/keylor-navas-now-has-spanish-citizenship|publisher=Real Madrid|access-date=3 December 2014|date=3 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213132148/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/12/keylor-navas-now-has-spanish-citizenship|archive-date=13 December 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Keylor Navas obtains Spanish nationality|url=https://www.marca.com/en/2014/12/03/en/football/real_madrid/1417633827.html|access-date=3 December 2014|work=Marca|date=3 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204002023/https://www.marca.com/en/2014/12/03/en/football/real_madrid/1417633827.html|archive-date=4 December 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Navas has been married to Andrea Salas since 2009, and the couple have three children together: Daniela, Mateo, and Thiago. Navas is the stepfather of Daniela, whom Andrea had in a previous relationship.<ref>{{cite web|title=Who is Andrea Salas? Meet Keylor Navas' wife who is a Costa Rican swimwear model and a former Miss Hawaiian Tropic|last=Mba|first=Nnanna|date=3 February 2023|url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/news-who-andrea-salas-meet-keylor-navas-wife-costa-rican-swimwear-model-former-miss-hawaiian-tropic|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

A documentary film, ''Hombre de Fe'' (Man of Faith), based on the life of Navas, was released on 28 December 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://qcostarica.com/hombre-de-fe-the-story-of-keylor-navas/|title=Hombre De Fé, The Story Of Keylor Navas|trans-title=Man of Faith, The Story of Keylor Navas|publisher=QCostaRica|language=es|date=28 December 2017|access-date=7 July 2018}}</ref>

His paternal half-brother, Eder Navas, is also a footballer who plays for Saprissa.<ref>{{cite news|last=Gómez|first=Keish|title=Keylor revela que su hermano Eder Navas formará parte del Saprissa|url=https://www.espn.co.cr/futbol/costa-rica/nota/_/id/9779438/keylor-navas-emotivo-mensaje-bienvenida-eder-saprissa|access-date=11 April 2022|work=ESPN.com.mx|date=13 January 2022|language=es}}</ref>

In 2022, Navas obtained his academic degree as a master in [[sport management]] from [[Johan Cruyff Institute]].<ref>{{cite web|date=9 October 2022|title=Keylor Navas is already preparing for life after being a professional footballer|url=https://www.archysport.com/2022/10/keylor-navas-is-already-preparing-for-life-after-being-a-professional-footballer/|access-date=11 October 2022|website=Archysport|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221011115636/https://www.archysport.com/2022/10/keylor-navas-is-already-preparing-for-life-after-being-a-professional-footballer/|archive-date=11 October 2022|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In June 2024, a report from [[BFM TV]] detailed that a former employee filed a complaint against Navas for [[Unreported employment|concealed work]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sellami|first1=Stéphane|last2=El Khaouafi|first2=Naoufel|last3=Couet|first3=Nicolas|date=5 June 2024|title=Info BFMTV. L'ex gardien du PSG Keylor Navas visé par une plainte d'un ancien employé pour travail dissimulé|url=https://rmcsport.bfmtv.com/football/ligue-1/info-bfmtv-le-gardien-du-psg-keylor-navas-vise-par-une-plainte-d-un-ancien-employe-pour-travail-dissimule_AV-202406050190.html|access-date=5 June 2024|website=BFMTV|language=fr}}</ref>

==Honours==
[[File:Real Madrid C.F. the Winner Of The Champions League in 2018 (1).jpg|thumb|400px|Navas (front row, with green uniform) celebrating Real Madrid's victory at the [[2018 UEFA Champions League final]]. He is one of seven goalkeepers to win the title a record three times.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los mejores porteros de la Champions League|url=https://es.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0e99cbb16882-2c85b50934cf-1000--los-mejores-porteros-de-la-champions-league/|website=[[UEFA]]|access-date=11 April 2022|language=es|date=25 February 2020}}</ref>]]
